title: Upper zone sensor open
shortDescription: Upper zone temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription: GE Profile wine coolers display Er1 when the upper zone thermistor reports an open or shorted reading. The cabinet falls back to a default set point until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the upper liner cover and reseat the sensor lead.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot reach the rear of the liner.

faq.a: It will hold a fail-safe temperature.

title: Lower zone sensor open
shortDescription: Lower zone thermistor reads out of range.
fullDescription: Er2 indicates the lower zone sensor reports out of range. The cabinet uses a default set point until repaired.
whenToCallPro: Call if liner access is unsafe.

faq.a: Yes briefly; fail-safe set point holds for a few days.

title: Evaporator sensor fault
shortDescription: Evaporator coil sensor reports out of range.
fullDescription: Er3 indicates the evaporator thermistor is open or shorted, preventing proper defrost cycling and risking frost build-up.
whenToCallPro: Many owners prefer a tech for evap work.

faq.a: Defrost cannot trigger without a valid sensor reading.

title: Door open alarm
shortDescription: Door has been open beyond alarm threshold.
fullDescription: Er4 alerts that the door has been open for several minutes. Verify the door magnet is aligned with the reed switch.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the door fully latches and seal is intact.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the door magnet aligns with the reed switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Replace reed switch if door is closed but Er4 persists.

faq.q: Why does it trip when closed?
faq.a: Magnet shift or failed reed switch.

title: Condenser fan fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan does not report speed.
fullDescription: Er5 indicates the condenser fan is not running. Dust, a loose plug, or worn motor are common causes.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Replace condenser fan if it does not spin freely.

whenToCallPro: Call if the unit is built into cabinetry.

title: Compressor over-current
fullDescription: Er6 trips when the compressor draws too much current. Restricted airflow, a failing start relay, or a worn compressor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Compressor service
fixSteps.instruction: If Er6 remains, the compressor needs service.

faq.a: Often yes for 5 years; check your paperwork.

title: Light circuit fault
shortDescription: Interior LED light driver reports a fault.
fullDescription: Er7 indicates the interior light driver detected a short or open. The cooler runs normally; only the lights are disabled.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the LED connector behind the side trim.

fixSteps.title: Replace LED
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the LED strip if dark.

whenToCallPro: Call if interior trim removal worries you.

faq.q: Is the cooler safe to use?
faq.a: Yes, only the lights are affected.

title: Communication error
shortDescription: Display board lost link to main control.
fullDescription: Er8 indicates the display and main board are not communicating. Loose connectors or a failed UI board are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the ribbon between the UI and main board.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the UI board if reseat fails.

whenToCallPro: Most owners should call a tech.

faq.a: Sometimes yes, but the user cannot adjust set point.

title: Cabinet too warm
shortDescription: Cabinet held above set point for over an hour.
fullDescription: HI alerts that the cabinet has been warmer than set point for an extended time. Causes include overload, hot ambient, or a sealed-system loss.

fixSteps.title: Service refrigerant
fixSteps.instruction: Call a sealed-system tech if HI persists.

title: Sabbath mode active
shortDescription: Sabbath mode disables lights and beeps.
fullDescription: Sb indicates the cooler is in Sabbath mode. The compressor still runs, but lights and tones are suppressed. Hold the temperature key for 5 seconds to exit.

fixSteps.title: Exit Sabbath
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the temperature key for 5 seconds.

faq.a: No, only lights and tones are affected.
